english.title: Fail / refuse to cause surrender of wireless telegraphy licence to OFCOM
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having a duty under section 11(1) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 to cause a wireless telegraphy licence to be surrendered to OFCOM, without reasonable excuse failed or refused to do so

english.notes:
(i) Section 11(1) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 provides that where a wireless telegraphy licence has expired or has been revoked, it is the duty of the person to whom the licence was granted, and any other person in whose possession or under whose control the licence may be, to cause it to be surrendered to OFCOM if required by them to do so.
(ii) Section 11(2) of the Act provides that section 11(1) does not apply to a licence that relates solely to receiving apparatus.
(iii) Section 105 of the Act makes special provisions for this offence in relation to ships and aircraft.
(iv) Section 106 of the Act applies where a person is convicted of this offence and the failure or refusal continues after the conviction.
(v) Section 107 of the Act provides for proceedings and enforcement where this offence has been committed in UK territorial sea.
(vi) Section 110 of the Act provides for criminal liability of company directors, managers, etc.
(vii) Schedule 4 of the Act provides for fixed penalty notices for this offence.
(viii) The Wireless Telegraphy (Fixed Penalty) Regulations 2011, (In force 01/10/2011), introduces a £100-00p fixed penalty charge for summary only offences under the Act, as from that date. This regime does not include offences relating to illegal broadcasting (pirate radio).
